perception_loop.assessment: Both sessions repeatedly rendered, adjusted, and rendered again. There were 11 render-bearing apply_ops/look calls in total: seven in stage0 and four in e1. Seven edit rounds followed an earlier render and were followed by another render, giving seven render→adjust→render loops. Neither session was a single-render session. The stage0 sequence was especially iterative: layout, crowding correction, connections, lint-driven label cleanup, a further cleanup, and a final whole-board look. The e1 sequence similarly rendered the new section, adjusted routing, adjusted c28 again, and then performed a final whole-board look.

lint_etiquette.assessment: Lint errors were fixed rather than fought. The first connected stage0 render introduced 10 errors, all of which were removed over two strategy-changing edits; e1 introduced three errors, all resolved over two routing edits. No identical lint was re-fired for more than three consecutive turns without a strategy change, so there was no lint fight. Both commits knowingly retained six warnings. Stage0 gave a concrete reason for its six retained warnings—long cross-section control/replay wires—while e1 named the six IDs but only called them existing/remaining routing warnings, without a specific verbatim diagnostic reason. Accordingly, six retained warnings are treated as reasoned and six as silently/unreasoned overridden for rubric purposes.
